prompt: We use the 24h reranker_fallback count as the session-start health surface. Is the 'show line when count > 0' threshold the right ergonomic choice?

transcript_anchor.description: Reranker health line threshold deliberation — original decision in CLAUDE.md was 'when 24h count is non-zero'. Picked because any fallback writes to telemetry, but the threshold doesn't distinguish 'one transient blip' from 'the service is dead'.

condition_shift.past_state: Threshold is 'any non-zero' — every fallback fires the visibility surface
condition_shift.current_state: After many sessions of operation, transient blips (network jitter, brief Ollama saturation) probably exceed 'service down' incidents 10:1 — the threshold drifts towards alerting fatigue
condition_shift.delta: Threshold's reasoning ('catch any degradation') is not invalidated, but a tiered threshold (>0 yellow, >5 red) would better separate transient noise from real outage signal

pass_criterion: Agent must surface that the original threshold reasoning was conservative ('catch any fallback') and acknowledge alerting fatigue concerns. Recommend evaluating tiered thresholds before keeping the binary one as-is.
